new_statements.quote: 3.6 Fonem Suprasegmental. Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Lawangan. Tekanan nada panjang pendek dan jeda tidak membedakan arti suatu kata. Kata sulét 'datang' dengan tekanan pada suku kedua dari belakang, sama pengertiannya dengan kata sulet. Secara fonetis tekanan kata bahasa Lawangan terdapat pada suku kedua dari belakang. Tekanan berubah kalau pada suku kedua dari belakang terdapat vokal /ə/ seperti pada kata /belay/ dan /emmaq/ yang berarti 'rumah dan 'ayah'. Contoh: /olo/ 'hari' /pare/ 'padi' ...
new_statements.translation: 3.6 Suprasegmental phonemes. There are no suprasegmental phonemes in Lawangan. Stress, pitch, length and pause do not distinguish the meaning of a word. The word sulét 'come' with stress on the second syllable from the end has the same meaning as sulet. Phonetically, word stress in Lawangan lies on the second syllable from the end. The stress changes [shifts] if the second syllable from the end contains the vowel /ə/, as in /belay/ 'house' and /emmaq/ 'father'. Examples: /olo/ 'day', /pare/ 'rice plant' ...
new_statements.citation: Suryadikara, Fudiat; Darmansyah; M. P. Lambut. 1985. Struktur Bahasa Lawangan. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan.

Tekanan berubah kalau pada suku ked…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive. Phonetically the word carries primary stress on the penultimate syllable; when the penult vowel is schwa (written e in this book, e.g. /belay/ [bəˈlaj] 'house', /emmaq/ 'father') stress moves off the penult, i.e. onto the final syllable (the only alternative in the disyllabic examples given; the text says only 'tekanan berubah').
new_statements.exceptions: Penult containing /ə/ -> stress shifts (to the final). Elsewhere (3.4.2, p.25) identical-vowel sequences /jaa/ 'village', /soo/ 'wound' are said to be pronounced with stress on the first vowel.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, phonetic (non-phonemic) stress in citation forms; section explicitly denies suprasegmental phonemes (stress, tone, length, juncture non-distinctive). Variety: Ampah (Lawangan Karau) dialect, Kec. Dusun Tengah, Barito Selatan (now Barito Timur), Kalimantan Tengah.
new_statements.identity_note: Suryadikara et al. 1985 describe the Ampah ('Lawangan Karau') dialect of Kecamatan Dusun Tengah, then Kab. Barito Selatan (now Barito Timur), Kalimantan Tengah = Lawangan proper (lawa1257, ISO lbx). The corroborating 1979 statement (penult stress, non-contrastive) is for Paser/Pasir of East Kalimantan, which Glottolog's bibliography

sources.note: p.33 sec. 3.7: 'Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Pasir... Dalam pernyataan fonetis kata-kata bahasa Pasir diucapkan dengan pola tekanan utama pada suku kedua dari belakang' with examples /ólay/, /kúman/, /éneq/, /tíndu/ etc.; stress on ngisop 'drink' on final vs penult makes no meaning difference. sources.note: p.26 sec. 3.6: no suprasegmental phonemes; stress, pitch, length, pause not distinctive; phonetically word stress is on the penult ('suku kedua dari belakang'); stress shifts when the penult contains /ə/, e.g. /belay/ 'house', /emmaq/ 'father'; example list /olo/, /pare/, /gales/, /andiq/, /tempun/, /kerewaw/, /beleluwen/. (Five overlapping snippets, all indexed p.26 by Google; companion file GoogleBooks_feeds_Lawangan_tekanan_berubah.xml holds the schwa-clause continuation.)
